newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds fines against tennis ball distributors.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds fines against tennis ball distributors.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance dismissed on Wednesday a plea from the Dutch sporting goods distributor Van Megen Sports to throw out fines imposed by the European Commission for violation of competition rules.

The Commission fined Van Megen and others, including Tretorn, for participating in a scheme to control the sales of Tretorn tennis balls by preventing parallel imports and exports of Tretorn balls by its distributors.

Van Megen challenged the Commission decision, saying it was based on insufficient evidence and lacked an adequate statement of reasons. Van Megen denied that Tretorn imposed an export ban on it or that it participated in a reporting of or investigation of parallel imports.
The court found telephone conversations between Tretorn and the applicant, initiated by Van Megen, supported a finding of active participation and the imposition of a fine.
(Court translation into Engish. Original language of the case: Dutch)
"Competition - Article 85 of the EC Treaty - Proof of the infringement - Fine - Statement of the reasons for the decision"
Van Megen Sports Group BV, applicant
Commission of the European Communities, defendant

application for annulment of Commission decision 94/987/EC of 21 December 1994 relating to a proceeding pursuant to article 85 of the EC Treaty (IV/32.948 - IV34.590: Tretorn and others) (OJ 1994 L 378, p. 45)
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby
2. Orders the applicant to pay the costs.
